lessons.title: Using 'But' to Show Contrast
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to join two contrasting ideas using 'but'.
success_criteria: I can complete a sentence using 'but'.
I can write my own sentence comparing old and new toys with 'but'.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models a sentence: 'Old toys were made of wood, but new toys are made of plastic.'
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model constructing 'but' sentences comparing old and new toys.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 'but' sentences comparing toys then and now.
key_questions: What is different between old and new toys?
Can you join your ideas with 'but'?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ varied 'but' sentences independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note use of conjunctions for contrast — evidence for ENG.W3.
lessons.plenary: Share 'but' sentences with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Make up a 'but' sentence comparing two things at home.

lessons.title: Venn Diagrams: Sorting Toys
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sort objects into a Venn diagram using two criteria.
success_criteria: I can sort a toy into the correct part of a Venn diagram.
I can explain my sorting.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sorting from earlier weeks.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce a simple two-circle Venn diagram (e.g. 'old' and 'wooden'), modelling sorting.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort toy picture cards into a Venn diagram (old/new, wooden/plastic), explaining overlaps.
key_questions: Where does this toy go?
Why does it go in the middle?

differentiation.greater_depth: Sort with 3 overlapping categories

lessons.assessment_notes: Note sorting/classifying skill using a Venn diagram — evidence for MATHS.MEA/GEO links.
lessons.plenary: Recap the Venn diagram sorting completed.
lessons.home_link: Sort toys or objects at home using two categories.

lessons.title: Direct Comparison: My Toy vs Grandparent's Toy
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to directly compare a modern toy to a toy from the past.
success_criteria: I can compare a modern toy to an old toy.
I can say one thing that is the same and one that is different.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap information gathered about family toys from previous weeks.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing a modern toy directly to a historical equivalent (e.g. modern doll vs rag doll).
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a comparison chart for a modern toy and its historical equivalent.
key_questions: What is the same about these toys?
What is different?

differentiation.support: Complete comparison with adult support, one similarity/difference
differentiation.greater_depth: Give 3+ similarities/differences independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note direct comparison skill, a key historical thinking skill — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Share comparisons made with the class.
lessons.home_link: Compare one of your toys to what a family member had as a child.

lessons.title: Old and New Toy Illustration Styles
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare illustration styles used in old and new toy catalogues/books.
success_criteria: I can notice a difference in illustration style.
I can say which style I prefer and why.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at an old toy catalogue/book illustration vs a modern one.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss differences in illustration style (colour use, detail, printing methods) between old and new.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw a toy in an 'old-fashioned' style (e.g. sepia/limited colour) and a 'modern' style, comparing.
key_questions: What do you notice about the old illustration?
How is the modern one different?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for style preferences in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe comparative artistic understanding — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Display both styles side by side and discuss.
lessons.home_link: Look at an old book or magazine illustration together if available.

lessons.title: Writing a Toy Comparison Paragraph
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a short paragraph comparing an old and new toy.
success_criteria: I can write 2-3 sentences comparing toys.
I can use 'but' or 'and' to join ideas.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Monday's 'but' sentences.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a short comparison paragraph using previously gathered information.
lessons.independent_task: Children write a short paragraph (2-3 sentences) comparing an old and new toy of their choice.
key_questions: What are you comparing?
How are they different?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ sentences with varied conjunctions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note extended writing and comparison skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share paragraphs with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Read your paragraph to your family.

lessons.title: Telling Time: O'Clock
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to tell the time to the hour on an analogue clock.
success_criteria: I can read o'clock times on a clock.
I can draw hands on a clock for a given o'clock time.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the parts of a clock.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading and setting o'clock times on a demonstration clock.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise reading and drawing o'clock times using individual clock faces.
key_questions: What time does this clock show?
Can you show me 3 o'clock?

differentiation.support: Focus on a few key o'clock times with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Read and set all 12 o'clock times confidently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record o'clock time-telling ability — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire o'clock time reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise telling o'clock times on a clock at home.

lessons.title: How Has Play Changed Over Time?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way that children's play has changed over time.
success_criteria: I can describe how play has changed.
I can give a reason why.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children do for fun today vs long ago.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss changes in play (more indoor/screen-based play now vs more outdoor play in the past), being balanced and non-judgemental.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and describe a way play has changed, giving a simple reason.
key_questions: How has play changed?
Why do you think this happened?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give reasoning involving technology/society changes

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of change over time and its causes — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap ways play has changed.
lessons.home_link: Ask a family member how they used to play as a child.

lessons.title: Creating a 'Then and Now' Toy Collage
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a collage comparing an old and new toy.
success_criteria: I can create a collage showing an old and new toy.
I can use different materials for each.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at collage examples.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a split collage - one side 'then', one side 'now' - using different textured materials.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a 'then and now' toy collage using varied materials (fabric for old, shiny paper for new, etc.).
key_questions: What materials show 'old'?
What materials show 'new'?

differentiation.support: Adult supports material choice and placement
differentiation.greater_depth: Add labels and detailed comparison notes

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe material choice reflecting comparison understanding — evidence for ART.1/HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Display 'then and now' collages together.
lessons.home_link: Look for old vs new material textures around your home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Comparison Sentences
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read simple comparison sentences fluently.
success_criteria: I can read a comparison sentence.
I can read it with increasing fluency.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap graphemes practised this term.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading comparison sentences containing target graphemes (e.g. 'the old toy is made of wood, but the new toy is not').
lessons.independent_task: Children practise reading a range of comparison sentence cards with increasing fluency.
key_questions: Can you read this sentence?
Can you read it more quickly?

differentiation.greater_depth: Read fluently and independently, then read to a partner

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reading fluency progress — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a fluency reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading comparison sentences over the week.

lessons.title: Telling Time: Half Past
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to tell the time to the half hour on an analogue clock.
success_criteria: I can read half past times on a clock.
I can draw hands for a given half past time.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap o'clock times from Tuesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading and setting half past times, discussing the minute hand position.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise reading and drawing half past times using individual clock faces.
key_questions: What time does this clock show?
Can you show me half past 6?

differentiation.support: Focus on a few key half past times with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Mix o'clock and half past times confidently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record half past time-telling ability — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire half past time reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise telling half past times on a clock at home.

lessons.title: Creating a Class Toy Timeline
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to contribute to a class timeline showing toys through time.
success_criteria: I can place a toy on the timeline in roughly the right place.
I can explain my reasoning.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the concept of a timeline from Week 3.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce a large class timeline spanning roughly 100+ years, discussing how to place toys on it.
lessons.independent_task: Children place a toy picture on the class timeline in the appropriate place, explaining their reasoning.
key_questions: Where does this toy go on the timeline?
Why did you place it there?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning using specific historical clues (material, style)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note chronological understanding — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Walk through the completed class timeline together.
lessons.home_link: Talk through the toy timeline with your family.

lessons.title: Designing a Museum Label
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to design and write a museum-style label for a toy artefact.
success_criteria: I can write a title for my toy.
I can write one fact about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at real museum labels (pictures/examples).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model designing a simple museum label including a title, date/era, and one fact.
lessons.independent_task: Children design and write a museum label for a toy from the week's learning (their own model, drawing, or a picture card).
key_questions: What will you title your label?
What fact will you include?

differentiation.greater_depth: Include 2+ facts and a designed border/decoration

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe design and factual writing combined — evidence for ART.1/ENG.W2/HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Display toys with their museum labels.
lessons.home_link: Design a museum label for one of your own toys.

lessons.title: Class Debate: Are Old or New Toys Better?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to state and justify an opinion with a simple reason.
success_criteria: I can say my opinion.
I can give one reason for it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's comparison learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model stating an opinion with a reason: 'I think new toys are better because they light up.'
lessons.independent_task: Children state and justify their opinion on old vs new toys in a class discussion/mini debate, taking turns to speak respectfully.
key_questions: What is your opinion?
Why do you think that?

differentiation.support: Adult provides sentence frame for opinion and reason
differentiation.greater_depth: Respond respectfully to a differing opinion

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ability to state and justify an opinion — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the range of opinions shared respectfully.
lessons.home_link: Discuss with your family whether they prefer old or new toys and why.

lessons.title: Introduction to Grouping and Sharing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve simple grouping and sharing problems using toys.
success_criteria: I can share toys equally between people.
I can group toys into equal sets.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sharing fairly from earlier learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model sharing a set of toy counters equally between 2-3 people, and grouping counters into equal sets.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve simple sharing and grouping problems using toy counters.
key_questions: How many each if we share fairly?
Can you group these into sets of 2?

differentiation.greater_depth: Solve sharing/grouping problems within 20

lessons.assessment_notes: Record early multiplication/division understanding — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire sharing and grouping quiz.
lessons.home_link: Practise sharing snacks or toys fairly at home.

lessons.title: Presenting Toy Research to the Class
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present a piece of toy research clearly to the class.
success_criteria: I can share one fact I learned this topic.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole topic's learning so far.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear, confident presentation.
lessons.independent_task: Children choose their favourite fact/artefact from the topic and present it briefly to a small group.
resources_needed: Work from across the topic for reference
key_questions: What was your favourite fact this topic?
Can you answer a question about it?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence to the whole class

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cumulative historical knowledge and presentation confidence — evidence for HIST.1/ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate everyone's toy research presentations.
lessons.home_link: Present your favourite fact to your family.

lessons.title: Toy Museum Poster Design
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to design a poster advertising a class toy museum exhibition.
success_criteria: I can design an eye-catching poster.
I can include key information (what, where, when).
lessons.starter_activity: Look at example museum/exhibition posters.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model designing a poster with a title, image, and key information.
lessons.independent_task: Children design a poster advertising the class 'Toy Museum' exhibition planned for Friday.
key_questions: What information does your poster need?
How will you make it eye-catching?

differentiation.support: Adult supports layout and information inclusion
differentiation.greater_depth: Add persuasive language and detailed illustration

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe design and information-inclusion skill — evidence for ART.1/ENG links.
lessons.plenary: Display posters around the school for the exhibition.
lessons.home_link: Invite your family to hear about the toy museum exhibition.

lessons.title: Toy Museum Exhibition Day: Presenting
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to confidently present their toy museum work to visitors.
success_criteria: I can talk about my toy museum contribution.
I can answer a visitor's question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap presentation skills practised this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Final preparation talk: discuss confidence, clear voice, and being proud of their work.
lessons.independent_task: Children present their toy museum contributions (models, comparisons, timeline entries, labels) to visitors or another class.
resources_needed: All toy museum work from the topic
key_questions: What would you like to tell a visitor?
What question might they ask?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present confidently and field unexpected questions

lessons.assessment_notes: Final spoken language and historical knowledge assessment for the topic — evidence for ENG.SL1/HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate a successful toy museum exhibition.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family about the toy museum exhibition.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Time, Sorting, Sharing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply time-telling, sorting, and sharing skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can tell o'clock and half past times.
I can sort using a Venn diagram.
I can share/group fairly.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of time-telling, Venn diagram sorting, and sharing/grouping.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations: telling time, Venn diagram sorting, sharing/grouping problems.
key_questions: What time is this?
Where does this go on the diagram?
How many each if shared fairly?

differentiation.greater_depth: Independent completion with extension challenges

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 4 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/N3.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising telling the time over the weekend.

lessons.title: Toys Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise the key learning from the whole toys topic.
success_criteria: I can name one thing I learned about toys in the past.
I can name one way toys have changed.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole topic from Week 2-4.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the whole topic's learning into key takeaways.
lessons.independent_task: Children contribute to a final class reflection page summarising what they learned about toys then and now.
key_questions: What is the most interesting thing you learned?
How have toys changed over time?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain multiple ideas with detailed reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Final topic assessment summarising HIST.1 progress across the whole toys topic.
lessons.plenary: Whole-class celebration of the completed toys topic.
lessons.home_link: Share everything you learned about toys this topic with your family.

lessons.title: Toy Museum Exhibition: Final Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to arrange and finalise their art contributions for the exhibition display.
success_criteria: I can arrange my work neatly for display.
I can talk about my favourite piece.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all art pieces created this topic (drawings, sculptures, collages, posters, labels).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how to arrange work neatly and attractively for a final display.
lessons.independent_task: Children help arrange the final 'Toy Museum' exhibition display combining all topic artwork.
resources_needed: All art produced during the topic
key_questions: Where should this piece go?
Which is your favourite piece from this topic?

differentiation.greater_depth: Suggest arrangement ideas and help others

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reflection on the topic's art progress overall — evidence for ART.1/ART.2 across the topic.
lessons.plenary: Whole-class and visitor celebration of the finished exhibition.
lessons.home_link: Bring your family to see the toy museum exhibition if possible, or share photos of it.
